title: Strict monotonicity of the Gaussian quantile
statement: Let $\Phi(t)=\int_{-\infty}^{t}e^{-x^2/2}/\sqrt{2\pi}\,dx$ be the standard Gaussian distribution function, and define $Q(\alpha)=\inf\{t\in\mathbb R: \alpha\le\Phi(t)\}$. Then $Q$ is strictly increasing on $(0,1)$; that is, $Q(\alpha)<Q(\beta)$ whenever $0<\alpha<\beta<1$.
hypotheses_covered: The quantile arguments lie in the open interval $(0,1)
replaced: Let $\Phi$ and $\varphi$ be the standard Gaussian distribution function and density, and put $Q=\Phi^{-1}$ and $I(p)=\varphi(Q(p))$ for $0<p<1$. The function $Q$ is strictly increasing on $(0,1)$.
